Evaluate JAGS formula using posterior samples

Source: R/JAGS-formula-predict.R
JAGS_evaluate_formula.Rd

Evaluates a JAGS formula on a posterior distribution obtained from a fitted model, through the formula design that JAGS_fit() stores for the formula parameter (the processed formula, factor levels and contrasts, and the standardization of predictors). Posterior or prior draws without a fit are evaluated through the same design, built by JAGS_formula_draws(). Fits created by BayesTools 0.3.0, which store no design, must be refitted: they stop with an error of class BayesTools_refit_required (see JAGS_validate_fit_contract()). Formula random effects can be evaluated for existing grouping levels when either standardized latent random effects and covariance hyperparameters were monitored via random_monitor(latent = TRUE), or the group-level coefficients were monitored via random_monitor(coefficients = TRUE); otherwise, and for random-effect blocks compiled as marginalized, conditional evaluation stops with an error of class BayesTools_refit_monitoring (also BayesTools_refit_required). In a random-effect block of a scalar-correlation structure (CS, HCS, AR1, HAR, or CAR) compiled group by group, the coefficients of index levels that a group does not have in the fitted data are drawn from their exact Gaussian conditional law given the observed levels. This draw is stochastic and follows set.seed(). Row-indexed external random-effect SD sources, such as random_sd_source("tau", shape = "row"), are evaluated from latent random effects only. Model generation automatically monitors the required latent effects for these blocks. The posterior samples must either contain source columns named tau[1], ..., tau[N]. When prediction data are supplied, fitted_rows must explicitly map each prediction row to its fitted observation index. Alternatively, the source must provide a parameter_source() values function for reconstructing row-wise source values from the posterior samples and supplied prediction data. An unavailable new-row evaluation of a posterior-indexed row source raises BayesTools_prediction_new_rows_unavailable (parent BayesTools_prediction_unavailable), with reason = "posterior_indexed_row_source", block, the displayed source label, affected prediction rows, and caller context. It applies where the source of the new rows is needed, under new_levels = "sample"; with new_levels = "zero" the new rows contribute zero and need no source. Missing or malformed mappings, invalid source values, and missing monitored columns retain their own errors. Literal expression() terms use the replayable subset documented by JAGS_formula() and are evaluated against prediction data using JAGS-style row indexing through i. Array expressions such as X[i, column[i]] pair the coordinates pointwise. Each index must contain finite positive integers within its array dimension; scalar indices repeat across a common nonzero vector length. One-index expressions retain ordinary vector indexing. Sampled parameter references are reconstructed separately for every posterior draw. Replaying a fitted formula restores the stored expression syntax, dependency classification, and fitted data snapshot. Supply an explicit expression-free formula to evaluate a selected subset without those offsets. Inline transformations, offsets, dot expansion, and arbitrary calls are not supported. Create transformed predictors as explicit columns in data. Selected existing terms retain fitted factor coding and variable order, including interactions requested with reversed variable order. Predictors outside the selected terms are not required. Expression-valued scalar point coefficients use valid monitors first, otherwise their retained declaration and owned model data. New prediction rows do not replace that owned data. Unsupported scalar replay, missing parents, cycles, and malformed values raise BayesTools_formula_point_unavailable; absent affected owners require refitting. This replay does not extend bridge prior-expression eligibility or establish a structural point law from constant draws.

JAGS_evaluate_formula(
  fit,
  formula = NULL,
  parameter,
  data = NULL,
  prior_list = NULL,
  formula_target = NULL,
  blocks = NULL,
  new_levels = NULL,
  fitted_rows = NULL
)

Arguments

fit

model fitted with JAGS_fit() with a formula for parameter, or posterior draws carrying its formula design (JAGS_formula_draws()).

formula

formula specifying the right hand side of the assignment (the left hand side is ignored). If NULL, the fitted formula stored in formula_design metadata is used. Whether the intercept values are log-transformed before computing the linear predictor is a property of the fitted formula: the "log(intercept)" flag stored in formula_design applies to every formula, also to an explicit one without the "log(intercept)" attribute. An explicit "log(intercept)" attribute that disagrees with the stored flag (TRUE for a fitted formula without a log intercept, or FALSE for one with it) stops with a BayesTools_formula_transform_unavailable error (reason "log_intercept_mismatch", fields explicit and stored) naming both values: omit the attribute or set it to the stored value.

parameter

name of the parameter created with the formula

data

data.frame containing predictors included in the formula. If NULL, versioned original-scale fitted source data from formula_design metadata are used.

prior_list

named list of prior distribution of parameters specified within the formula. If NULL, fitted priors from formula_design metadata are used.

formula_target

formula prediction target. "fixed" evaluates only the fixed formula contribution. "conditional" evaluates fixed effects plus fitted or explicitly generated random-effect contributions. NULL (the default) evaluates the fixed formula of fits without random effects and stops for fits with random effects, which need an explicit target.

blocks

optional random-effect block names used with formula_target = "conditional". When formula has random-effect terms, the default is the blocks of those terms and supplied blocks must be among them.

new_levels

optional new-level policy used only with formula_target = "conditional". Use a random_new_levels() object or one of "error", "zero", or "sample". Grouping levels declared in the fitted grouping factor but without rows in the fitting data are predicted as new levels, except in blocks with a known group covariance; see prior_random().

fitted_rows

optional integer vector mapping supplied prediction rows to fitted observation indices. It is required whenever data is supplied and a selected random-effect block uses a posterior-indexed row source. Reordering and duplicate indices are supported. Callback-computed row sources do not use this mapping. The entries of rows of new random-effect levels predicted with new_levels = "zero" are ignored, because those rows contribute zero; they must still be valid fitted observation indices.

Value

JAGS_evaluate_formula returns a matrix of the evaluated posterior samples on the supplied data.

See also

JAGS_fit() JAGS_formula()
